problem: World models struggle with a memory trade-off where transformers preserve details but hit quadratic attention limits, while recurrent and state-space models scale efficiently but compress history and lose fidelity.
approach: Integrate multiple specialized memory experts through a diffusion-based framework with contrastive product-of-experts: a short-term expert for local dynamics, a long-term expert storing episodic history via lightweight finetuning, and a spatial expert for geometric coherence.
contribution: Compositional design avoids mode collapse, scales to long contexts without quadratic cost, and improves temporal consistency, recall of past observations, and navigation performance.

problem: KL divergence and f-divergence regularization in RLHF only compare token probabilities at identical positions, missing semantic similarity between tokens.
approach: Propose Wasserstein Policy Regularization (WPR) using entropy-regularized Wasserstein distance to capture token space geometry, with dual formulation yielding tractable penalty terms compatible with standard RL algorithms.
contribution: WPR outperforms KL and f-divergence baselines by incorporating semantic-aware policy distances for LLM alignment.

problem: Current LLMs generate bland, persona-misaligned role-playing dialogue despite strong reasoning, and RAG or scalar-reward RL cannot capture nuanced character-specific preferences across diverse contexts.
approach: Introduce R4, a unified framework equipping both reward model and agent with reasoning and retrieval: the reward reformulates evaluation as structured multi-step reasoning with retrieved knowledge, then supervises dialogue agent with same dual capabilities.
contribution: R4 substantially improves persona fidelity, narrative coherence, and emotional expressiveness, with agents achieving emergent role-playing behaviors unattainable by prior methods.

problem: Psychiatric comorbidity is clinically complex yet lacks large-scale dialogue datasets to support multi-disorder screening in realistic conversations.
approach: Create synthetic EMRs via a clinical-grounded pipeline, then generate multi-agent diagnostic dialogues through a hierarchical state machine supporting 130+ diagnostic states, validated by psychiatrists.
contribution: Construct PsyCoTalk, the first large-scale 3,000-dialogue comorbidity dataset with high structural and linguistic fidelity and confirmed diagnostic validity.

problem: Models can lie when interrogated about hidden objectives, making direct interrogation an unreliable safety technique.
approach: Self-report fine-tuning (SRFT) trains models to admit factual mistakes in QA, generalizing out-of-distribution to admission of hidden misaligned objectives in adversarial settings.
contribution: SRFT enables interrogation to detect hidden objectives with F1=0.98 vs baseline 0, and recover 28-100% objective details vs 0% in baseline.

problem: Depth cameras are inaccurate and noisy for robotic manipulation, limiting policies trained on depth to sim-only deployment.
approach: Develop Camera Depth Models (CDMs) as a neural data engine that generates paired high-quality depth data from simulation by modeling camera noise patterns, bridging sim-to-real for manipulation.
contribution: Policies trained on raw simulated depth without noise augmentation or real finetuning generalize seamlessly to real robots on long-horizon tasks with reflective and slender objects.

problem: Unlearning methods exhibit unstable trade-offs between forgetting and model utility, producing incoherent outputs and failing to suppress lexical and semantic associations in attention.
approach: Attention Smoothing Unlearning (ASU) casts unlearning as self-distillation from a forget-teacher by increasing softmax temperature to flatten attention and suppress associations.
contribution: ASU outperforms baselines on TOFU, MUSE, and WMDP with robust unlearning and minimal utility loss across QA and text completion.

problem: Federated fine-tuning of LLMs with heterogeneous client LoRA ranks suffers from initialization and aggregation noise, hurting performance.
approach: Fed-PLoRA replaces multi-rank LoRA with parallel one-rank modules and uses Select-N-Fold to fold untrained modules into pre-trained weights before local training.
contribution: Fed-PLoRA consistently outperforms existing methods in accuracy and efficiency across diverse LLM fine-tuning tasks on heterogeneous resources.

problem: There is a long-standing gap between provable L2 robustness certificates and empirical L-infinity robustness in adversarial defense.
approach: HyCAS couples 1-Lipschitz spectrally normalized convolutions with spectral-normalized random projections and randomized attention noise to achieve an overall ≤2-Lipschitz network with formal certificates.
contribution: HyCAS boosts certified accuracy by up to 7.3% and empirical robustness by up to 3.1% while maintaining clean accuracy across imaging benchmarks.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle with visual mathematical reasoning because extracted visual cues are not faithfully integrated or properly used in reasoning.
approach: CogFlow uses a cognitive-inspired three-stage framework: perception with synergistic visual rewards, internalization with visual-anchored reward models to bridge perception-reasoning, and reasoning with visual-gated policy optimization.
contribution: Contribute MathCog dataset with 120K+ perception-reasoning aligned annotations and achieve improved visual grounding in mathematical reasoning.

problem: Fairness methods either use task-specific constraints limiting generalizability or reduce prediction-attribute dependence via distance measures sensitive to choice of measure.
approach: Model-agnostic framework leveraging Cauchy-Schwarz Divergence as a principled measure of dependence to encourage prediction-attribute independence via optimization.
contribution: CS Divergence provides tighter theoretical bounds than alternative measures, unifying prior fairness efforts under a consistent principle.

problem: Non-autoregressive language models struggle to accurately model dependencies in discrete sequences despite efficiency gains.
approach: Apply conditional flow matching with KL divergence geodesics (linear interpolation in logit space) and propose sampling-hybrid inference iteratively denoising and re-noising.
contribution: Improves perplexity and downstream metrics over NAR baselines for unconditional and conditional text and code infilling.

problem: Memory benchmarks rely on static off-policy data limiting evaluation reliability and scalability for long-horizon assistant interactions.
approach: AMemGym provides interactive on-policy evaluation environment with structured data sampling for user profiles and state evolution, enabling cost-effective high-quality interaction generation.
contribution: Reveals performance gaps in existing memory systems (RAG, long-context LLMs, agentic memory) and enables diagnostically rich assessment of memory management.

problem: Existing fingerprinting approaches lack theoretical guidance for determining how far fingerprints should be from decision boundaries to satisfy robustness and uniqueness simultaneously.
approach: AnaFP formulates fingerprint generation as controlling fingerprint-to-boundary distance via a tunable stretch factor with mathematically formalized robustness and uniqueness constraints.
contribution: Establish theoretical bounds defining an admissible interval for stretch factor and enable practical fingerprint generation with surrogate model pools.

problem: Web agents struggle to engage in cognitive reasoning because they lack sufficient structured knowledge of websites.
approach: Web-CogKnowledge Framework categorizes knowledge into Factual/Conceptual/Procedural domains and operationalizes acquisition via knowledge-driven Chain-of-Thought reasoning.
contribution: Construct Web-CogDataset from 14 real-world websites with systematic knowledge curation, training Web-CogReasoner agent with significant superiority over existing models.

problem: Multimodal LLMs using fixed patch sizes suffer degraded performance at variable resolutions and incur high computational costs for high-resolution inputs.
approach: Adaptive Patching (AdaPatch) adjusts patch size by resolution and information density, plugging into pre-trained fixed-patch MLLMs without training.
contribution: Delivers consistent improvements in native resolution performance with up to 2x throughput boost and 4x reduction in prefilling time.

problem: Forward-pass attention alone unreliably distinguishes hallucinated from correct outputs in vision-language models.
approach: LVLMs-Saliency uses gradient-aware diagnostics fusing attention weights with gradients to quantify output token grounding, then applies saliency-guided rejection sampling and local coherence reinforcement.
contribution: Significantly reduces hallucinations via inference-time filtering and module-based attention strengthening, offering interpretable hallucination detection.

problem: The intuition that flat minima offer adversarial robustness is only partially correct and lacks formal justification.
approach: Rigorously formalize the relationship between flatness and robustness, deriving closed-form expressions and showing flatness implies local but not global robustness.
contribution: Prove loss must curve sharply away from data manifold for global robustness, revealing that adversarial examples lie in large flat regions where models are confidently wrong.

problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards requires massive data and extensive rollout computations, limiting data efficiency and training cost.
approach: DEPO combines offline data curation by diversity/influence/difficulty with online sample-level explorability filtering to reduce rollout costs, plus replay for under-explored samples.
contribution: Achieve 1.85x speedup on AIME24 and 1.66x speedup on AIME25 using only 20% of training data compared to GRPO on full dataset.

problem: Unlearnable Examples fail against pretrained models because pretraining priors bypass the shortcuts in perturbations and access true semantics.
approach: BAIT formulates a bi-level optimization where inner level mirrors UE objectives while outer level binds perturbations to incorrect labels, mislabeling pretraining priors.
contribution: Produce Unlearnable Examples that remain effective against pretraining priors across standard benchmarks and multiple pretrained backbones.

problem: Self-re-watermarking attacks, where the same encoder reembeds a new message into already watermarked images, defeat existing watermarking methods.
approach: Extend Lipschitz constraints to watermarking to limit model sensitivity, combined with re-watermarking adversarial training to constrain sensitivity to distortions.
contribution: Provide theoretical bounds on message recoverability under malicious re-embedding and demonstrate defense effectiveness.

problem: Standard pooling methods like mean or max aggregation treat tokens as independent, discarding the relational structure captured by self-attention.
approach: GLOT, a lightweight pooling module, constructs latent token-similarity graphs, refines representations with GNNs, then aggregates using readout layers.
contribution: Maintains 97% accuracy when 90% of tokens are distractors, competitive with SOTA on GLUE/MTEB with 20x fewer parameters and 100x faster than parameter-efficient finetuning.

problem: Low-bit activation quantization sharply degrades accuracy in LVMs and LLMs.
approach: STaMP applies linear transformations along sequence dimension to exploit local correlation, keeping small token sets at higher precision via mixed precision.
contribution: Significantly improve low bit-width activation quantization on recent LVM and LLM architectures, complementing existing quantization methods.

problem: Parallel LLM inference generates responses independently, partitioning compute and leaving information in one generation untapped by others.
approach: Bridge treats batched hidden states as holistic tensors rather than independent slices, enabling interdependent parallel generation with only 2.8-5.1% new parameters.
contribution: Improve RL with verifiable rewards accuracy gains by up to 39% and boost consistency, scaling to any generation width with better performance than independent generation.

problem: Existing acceleration methods focus on reducing image tokens in the LLM stage, overlooking bottlenecks in the image encoder which is the primary token contributor.
approach: iLLaVA jointly optimizes image encoder and LLM with token merging strategy recycling information from discarded tokens, achieving comprehensive end-to-end acceleration.
contribution: Deliver 2x throughput boost and 4x reduction in prefilling time, enabling larger models to surpass smaller counterparts in both accuracy and efficiency.

problem: Most approaches treat 3D geometric reconstruction and semantic understanding in isolation, overlooking their crucial interplay and limiting generalization.
approach: IGGT, an end-to-end transformer unifying geometry and instance-level understanding via 3D-Consistent Contrastive Learning guided by 2D visual inputs.
contribution: Construct InsScene-15K dataset with high-quality annotations and support consistent lifting of 2D inputs into coherent 3D scenes with distinct object instances.

problem: Conventional MNL bandits model relevance-driven choice but ignore within-assortment diversity, while submodular bandits encode diversity but lack structured choice probabilities.
approach: DMNL contextual bandit augments MNL choice probabilities with submodular diversity function, with OFU-DMNL algorithm building assortments item-wise by optimizing optimistic marginal gains.
contribution: Achieve (1-1/(e+1))-approximate regret bound with improved approximation factor over submodular baselines and comparable regret with substantially lower runtime.

problem: Watermark-based detection identifies AI-generated content but attribution to specific users remains largely unexplored.
approach: Assign unique watermarks to each user, embed them in content, then perform attribution by identifying best-matching watermarks, with theoretical optimization of user watermark selection.
contribution: Demonstrate watermark-based attribution remains accurate for unmodified or common post-processed content and resistant to limited-query adversarial post-processing.

problem: Time series forecasting reaches diminishing returns in accuracy; deployed models cannot improve accuracy and uncertainty without retraining.
approach: δ-Adapter, a lightweight architecture-agnostic post-processor with input nudging and output residual correction, learns bounded modules at encoder-LLM interfaces.
contribution: Improve accuracy and calibration with negligible compute and no interface changes, with local descent guarantees and compositional stability.

problem: Multi-agent RL methods for order dispatching either fail to capture global information or suffer curse of dimensionality; centralized methods struggle with vast observation and action spaces.
approach: Triple-BERT, a centralized single-agent RL method with action decomposition and BERT-based parameter reuse via attention, handles extensive driver-order relationships.
contribution: Achieve 11.95% improvement over state-of-the-art with 4.26% increase in ride fulfillment on real Manhattan ride-hailing data.

problem: Global noise variance in randomized smoothing creates a fundamental limitation: no single variance achieves strong robustness at both small and large radii.
approach: Dual RS framework enables input-dependent noise variances via variance estimator predicting optimal noise per input, independently smoothed via RS to ensure local constancy.
contribution: Achieve strong performance at both small and large radii unattainable with global variance, with 60% inference overhead.

problem: Forecasting motion from a single image without observing velocities or forces requires modeling scene-wide dynamics and uncertainty, which video generators struggle with.
approach: Formulate as conditional generation of dense trajectory grids using video generator architecture modified to output motion trajectories instead of pixels.
contribution: Capture scene-wide dynamics and uncertainty more accurately and diversely than prior regressors and generators, showing video generators poorly forecast motion.

problem: Deep learning crowd simulation methods suffer from error accumulation and low efficiency because they model crowds as independent trajectories, ignoring macroscopic physical laws.
approach: STDDN couples microscopic trajectory prediction with macroscopic physics via Neural ODE modeling density evolution driven by individual movements, using continuity equation constraints.
contribution: Physically regularize microscopic prediction, mitigate error accumulation, and improve simulation stability and efficiency.

problem: Mathematical modeling is time-intensive and expert-dependent, with challenges in handling modeling uncertainty, conflicting objectives, and subjective quality assessment.
approach: MATHMO conceptualizes modeling as sequential decision-making under uncertainty with bi-level search: high-level exploration across frameworks and local intra-framework refinements using LLMs.
contribution: Successfully discover Pareto-efficient frontiers of models balancing varied objectives including subjective criteria on diverse real-world tasks.

problem: Training-free latent reasoning in LLMs broadens search distribution causing probability mass diffusion and noise, while overthinking persists wasting tokens.
approach: SwiReasoning dynamically switches between explicit and latent reasoning guided by block-wise confidence from entropy trends, limiting maximum switches to curb overthinking.
contribution: Improve accuracy by 1.5-2.8% across reasoning LLMs and improve token efficiency by 56-79% under constrained budgets.

problem: LLM fingerprints using fixed query sets with atypical keys memorization do not survive deployment steps like finetuning or quantization and are easily detected.
approach: Replace fixed query sets with semantic domains and fixed keys with statistical watermarking signals diffused throughout responses via semantic conditioning.
contribution: Fingerprint is both stealthy and robust to all common deployment scenarios including finetuning and quantization.

problem: Vision-language models show demographic biases but the role of training data composition remains unclear due to lack of demographic annotations in large-scale datasets.
approach: Create person-centric annotations for LAION-400M including 276 million bounding boxes, perceived gender/race labels, and captions via validated automatic labeling pipelines.
contribution: Uncover demographic imbalances and harmful associations, showing 60-70% of gender bias in CLIP and Stable Diffusion traces to data co-occurrences.

problem: Existing universal gradient methods require knowing problem-specific parameters, limiting applicability across diverse problem classes.
approach: DADA, a parameter-free universal method based on dual averaging, dynamically adjusts coefficients via observed gradients and distance to starting point.
contribution: Simultaneously work for diverse problem classes including Lipschitz, smooth, Hölder-smooth, quasi-self-concordant functions without parameter tuning.

problem: Auto-regressive generation in sequence prediction requires quadratic time, with standard convolutional models not offering efficient generation alternatives.
approach: FutureFill, a general-purpose fast generation method for convolutional sequence models, reduces generation time from quadratic to quasilinear via dynamic programming.
contribution: Requires prefill cache growing only with tokens to generate and demonstrates substantial efficiency gains on language modeling.

problem: Current guardrail models address general human-LLM interactions but render LLMs vulnerable to harmful content in domain-specific contexts with technical jargon.
approach: ExpGuard, a robust specialized guardrail model designed for financial, medical, and legal domains, trained on ExpGuardMix, a curated 58,928-prompt dataset with domain expert validation.
contribution: Deliver competitive performance on established benchmarks while demonstrating exceptional resilience to domain-specific adversarial attacks, surpassing WildGuard by up to 15.3%.
